newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan port practices interim pact reached-ministry.
newsitem.headline: Japan port practices interim pact reached-ministry.

text.p: Japan's Transport Ministry said on Tuesday that a preliminary agreement had been reached between the Japan Harbour Transport Association and Japanese and foreign shipowners to reform certain Japanese port practices.

A Transport Ministry official said the parties had agreed to work towards the simplification and modernisation of the so-called prior consultation system and to come to a conclusion by the end of July.

This follows a decision by the U.S. Federal Maritime Commission, angry at what it says are costly and discriminatory practices at Japanese ports, to slap $100,000 surcharges from April 14 on vessels of Kawasaki Kisen, Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd and Nippon Yusen KK every time they stop at a U.S. port.

The FMC charged that Japan's Transport Ministry discourages applications for cargo handling licences and that the need to consult the JHTA for changes in all vessel operations, no matter how minor, gives the JHTA effective control over port business in Japan.
The ministry official said the ministry hoped the preliminary agreement would help persuade the United States to postpone the implementation of the sanctions.
"We believe the United States will be understanding. It is clear that (port) conditions will become much better than they are now," he said.

Part of the interim pact stipulates which items would need to be approved by the JHTA, and allows the Transport Ministry to step in to guide discussions if the parties fail to agree on changes to the operation of the prior consultation system.

The ministry official said that Japanese officials hope to meet U.S. authorities again as soon as possible before April 14, the date the sanctions come into effect. But he added that no specific date had been determined as the U.S. side needs time to assess the preliminary agreement.
